title: Kinetic slope rollout operator for smooth progressive ramps
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: implement a policy engine/operator named 'kinetic slope' that drives progressive traffic ramps for model rollouts with smooth rate-of-change limits, robust guardrails, and statistically principled auto-rollback. This ticket covers spec, runtime control loops, and an initial implementation for Redwood Dedicated and Hosted routes. The kinetic slope approach treats traffic percentage as a continuous variable with a configurable slope (pct/min) and enforces safety using sequential hypothesis tests (SPRT) on key metrics and hysteresis windows to avoid flip-flopping. It complements existing step-based schedulers by providing fine-grained throttling for low-latency, high-concurrency workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc (linked) reviewed and approved by PM and SRE
Runtime implements kinetic slope limiter and exposes DSL knobs (slope, max-step, min-hold)
Safety tests: SPRT-based metric checks for latency, error-rate, and quality regression pass in simulation harness
Auto-rollback triggers after configurable consecutive SPRT failures with cooldown and manual override
Integration with Console: real-time traffic curve visualization and one-click pause/rollback
End-to-end e2e scenario executed on staging: gradual ramp from 0% to 40% following slope policy with injected fault leading to rollback
rollout_policy_spec: kinetic_slope: { slope_pct_per_min: 5, max_step_pct: 10, min_hold_minutes: 3, watchdog_window_minutes: 5, sprt_alpha: 0.05, sprt_beta: 0.1, metrics: ["latency_p95","error_rate","quality_score"], rollback_conditions: ["sprt_failures>=2","latency_p95>300ms for 3m"], cooldown_minutes: 15 }
telemetry_requirements: Continuous comparison stream between control and candidate with SPRT outcomes
Traffic curve logs (timestamp,tgt_pct,actual_pct,decision,reason) persisted to telemetry index
Audit trail for manual overrides with actor and justification
runbook_steps: Start rollout with slope parameter and target max percentage
Monitor Console 'Traffic Curve' and SPRT status panel
If SPRT flags a metric, operator automatically pauses ramp for min_hold and re-evaluates
On second consecutive SPRT failure, auto-rollback to previous stable variant and notify on-call
If operator pauses but metrics recover within watchdog_window, resume ramp at half the previous slope
Manual path: SRE/PM may force-pause or force-rollback; all actions appended to audit log
design_notes: Rationale: step-based ramps are coarse for traffic-sensitive apps. Kinetic slope ensures smoother backend load transitions and reduces bursty resource pressure.
Use SPRT (Sequential Probability Ratio Test) to minimize sample size needed to detect quality/latency regressions and avoid false positives in low-traffic canaries.
Hysteresis and cooldown are required to prevent oscillation when metrics hover near thresholds; we adopt a two-tier failure policy (probe-level pause, then rollback).
Support shadow probing by sampling a configurable shadow_pct stream; shadow samples evaluate quality_score without affecting user-visible traffic.
Expose conservative defaults (slope=1%/min, max_step=5%) and allow aggressive profiles for enterprise customers with SLOs and budget tradeoffs.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SPRT sensitivity on very small sample sizes may trigger unwarranted pauses. Mitigation: enforce minimum sample thresholds and default to shadow probe aggregation for low-QPS rollouts.
Risk: Improper slope could overload dependent services. Mitigation: integrate with service-level admission controller that respects backend capacity annotations.
Risk: Audit/approval gaps for auto-rollback. Mitigation: require two-person approval to disable auto-rollback for a release; log all exceptions.

Risk: Complexity in multi-variant A/B experiments. Mitigation: treat kinetic slope as orthogonal to experiment traffic allocation; only applicable to candidate->control progressive promotions, not multi-arm randomization
